stage1.impression: A warm, softly lit minimalist living room with the green acrylic horn pair flanking a walnut credenza; the palette is pleasant, but it reads at once as an archviz render: the rug is a flat board, the armchair's cushions are stacked boxes, the window shows a blank block, and the hardest light falls on the chair rather than the product. The speakers are small in frame, murky in the cabinets and unequal (the right one sits in the dim half), and they throw no green light onto the floor, so they read as furniture in a catalogue room, not the hero.

blocking_9: No placeholder or broken assets: one seat and one back cushion on the chair with seams and weave, a rug with real pile and a soft edge, a real exterior through the window, real walnut veneer on the credenza, a real turntable and books.

The pair is lit by the scene's sun: the tinted acrylic visibly transmits light and each speaker lays a green-tinted pool and a firm contact shadow on the floor (lower cabinets at median 65-75 or more, not 35-41).
The two speakers read as a matched pair: horn-wing and cabinet medians within about 15% of each other (horn wings are 161 vs 82 now).
The pair is the highest-contrast, most luminous zone of the frame, not the sunlit floor by the chair (median 205, range 140).
The pair spans at least half the frame height at equal size, with no dead dark foreground, no tangents between rug edges and speaker feet, and clear wall for 'A pair of Poison.'
Every large surface carries real micro-detail: floor grain (100-px lum range 16 or more), rug pile (12 or more), wall plaster.
The cabinets read as specified (tinted acrylic over a white lining) and the green matches the product reference; both need the product asset checked, which is out of scope here.

defects.what: Rug is a flat, untextured slab with a hard laminated double edge (100-px patches lum range 4.1 and 2.1); reads as a sheet of board and fills the bottom quarter of the frame as dead dark weight (median 81).
Rug's back edge runs 12-30 px in front of the left speaker's feet and its back-right corner stops about 30 px from the right speaker's front-left foot: tangents.
Armchair cushions are duplicated, offset box slabs (two back, three seat) with 90-degree edges: broken placeholder geometry sitting in the strongest light.
Window exterior is a flat beige block (lum range 1.0) under a blank sky: placeholder.
Sheer curtains are evenly repeated vertical pleats with no weave, sway or hem detail.
Credenza veneer is a procedural wave pattern repeated identically across the three doors, near-black and matte (median 48.9, range 9.7).
Turntable and books are low-detail models: box plinth, plain platter, blank spines.
Oak floor is smooth and almost grainless (100-px patches lum range 7.6-8.4), hairline joints, no bevels, no reflections.
Wall is perfectly smooth paint with no plaster texture (300 x 200 px patch range 4.0).
The highest-contrast zone is the sunlit floor and chair at left (median 204.6, range 139.8), pulling the eye away from the pair.
Light falls off from left to right across the back wall (236 to 153), leaving the right speaker in the dim half.
Right speaker reads half as bright and more olive than the left (horn wing median 81.9, RGB 80,87,40 vs 161.4, RGB 150,169,118).
Left cabinet reads murky dark olive (front median 60.6, lower 41.2, blue 7-18); no transmitted glow.
Right cabinet darker still (front median 52.7, lower 34.8, blue 4-16).
No green transmitted light on the floor in front of the left speaker (g/r 0.72 vs 0.76 on bare floor); contact shadow only ~8 px deep.
No green on the floor in front of the right speaker (g/r 0.69 vs 0.71 on bare floor).
Left woofer cloth cover reads as a flat plastic disc (lum range 7.8); product shader.
Right woofer cloth cover flat (lum range 2.9); product shader.
Print's green band (RGB 92,100,70) repeats the product's green between the pair, diluting it as the one green in the room.
Second vase of twigs repeats the centre vase motif and crowds the right speaker.
Camera yaw makes the pair unequal in size (653 vs 745 px tall) and small (40-46% of frame height); a downward shift adds floor.

changes.problem: The pair stands outside the scene's only strong light: the sunbeam stops at the chair, so the cabinets read as murky dark olive, transmit nothing and throw no green onto the floor, while the chair corner is the hardest-lit thing in the frame.

evidence.measured: Lower right cabinet lum_median 34.8 (blue 4); lower left [790,1100,1045,1200] 41.2 (blue 7); cabinet fronts 52.7 and 60.6; floor in front of the left speaker g/r 0.72 vs 0.76 on bare floor (no green); sunlit floor by the chair [0,1300,600,1560] median 204.6.

change.from: beam lands only on the floor around the armchair (x < 700); sheers drawn over the rear bay
change.to: sheers opened; sun elevation about 15 degrees, azimuth about 25 degrees off the back-wall plane, still from back-left (shadows toward camera-right as now), so the beams through the rear and front bays cross the lower half of both cabinets and the floor in front of them; colour about 5000 K so the tint is not pushed to olive

changes.expected: Both lower cabinets glow green (right 65 or more, left 75 or more, from 35 and 41); each speaker lays a long green-tinged shadow pool toward camera-right on the floor and rug; contact shadows firm up; the chair corner stops being the hardest-lit zone.

changes.problem: The rug is a perfectly flat, untextured slab with a hard laminated double edge that fills the bottom quarter of the frame and runs tangent to both speakers' feet.

evidence.measured: lum_range 4.1 in this 100-px patch and 2.1 at [1600,1400,1700,1500]; rug median 81 over [600,1380,1500,1600]; back edge 12-30 px in front of the left speaker's feet, back-right corner about 30 px from the right speaker's front-left foot.

change.from: flat dark-taupe slab with a bevelled board edge, back edge tangent to both speakers
change.to: hand-knotted or tufted wool rug in oatmeal or warm ivory, 12-15 mm pile from a scanned texture with displacement (tufts 3-5 mm), soft bound edge relaxing onto the floor with slight waviness, 2.5 x 3.5 m centred on the credenza, back edge 300 mm clear in front of the speakers' feet

changes.expected: Pile and fibre read in the foreground (100-px patches lum range 12 or more); the rug lifts to a median of about 120-150 so the bottom of the frame stops reading as a dark dead mass and bounces warm light into the cabinets; no tangents.

changes.problem: The armchair's cushions are duplicated, offset hard-edged boxes (two back slabs, three seat slabs), the loudest render tell in the frame.

evidence.measured: At 2x the back cushion is two offset slabs and the seat three stacked offset slabs, all with 90-degree edges; back-cushion face [240,800,440,930] lum_range 18.4 with no form, seams or weave.

change.from: placeholder walnut-frame chair with duplicated box cushions
change.to: a high-detail production or scanned lounge chair: solid walnut frame, one seat and one back cushion in wool boucle or heavy linen, sewn seams, 15-20 mm rounded edges, soft crown and light sitting creases; same position and scale

changes.expected: One seat and one back cushion with soft form, seams and visible weave; shading follows the cushions' curvature; nothing intersects.

changes.problem: Light falls off across the room, so the right speaker sits in the dim half and reads half as bright and more olive than the left; the pair does not match.

evidence.measured: Right horn wing lum_median 81.9, RGB 80,87,40 vs left [765,575,860,735] 161.4, RGB 150,169,118; back-wall profile [400,100,2880,200] along x falls from 236.0 to 153.4 (falloff 82.6); wall beside the right speaker 132 vs 178 beside the left.

change.from: none: the room is lit from the left glazing only
change.to: a second, sun-free window on the right wall just out of frame (or a 2 x 2.5 m diffuse daylight panel 3 m right of camera, 1.5 m high), about 5500 K, at about half the left window's intensity, so the right half of the back wall comes within about 15% of the left

changes.expected: Back-wall falloff across the frame 35 levels or less; right horn wing 110 or more and within about 25% of the left; the right cabinet's green matches the left's.

changes.problem: Shot from about 1.3 m with a roughly 35 mm-equivalent lens yawed about 13 degrees off the back wall and shifted down, the pair is small and unequal in size and a quarter of the frame is foreground rug.

evidence.measured: Left speaker 653 px tall (40% of frame height), right 745 px (46%), ratio 1.14; the rug's sides converge at about (2100, 545) and the baseboard runs to a vanishing point far left, giving a camera about 1.3 m high, about 35 mm, yawed about 13 degrees, with the horizon 265 px above frame centre (downward shift); rug and floor fill y 1225-1620.

change.from: about 1.3 m high, about 35 mm, yawed about 13 degrees left of the back-wall normal, shifted down (horizon at y 545)
change.to: 1.05 m high, level with no vertical shift (horizon near mid-frame), squared to the back wall (yaw 3 degrees or less), 40 mm, distance set so each speaker spans about 50% of frame height; keep the credenza and part of the armchair in frame as scale references and the wall above the left speaker clear for the heading

changes.expected: Each speaker about 800 px tall and within 3% of the other; floor and rug 15% of the frame or less; horns just above eye level. Render this pass after the other changes' region tests have passed, then re-anchor those regions.

changes.problem: The credenza's walnut is a procedural pattern of identical wavy bands repeated across all three doors, near-black and matte, and the turntable and books on it are low-detail models.

evidence.measured: Doors lum_median 48.9, lum_range 9.7, RGB 78,44,12; the same wave bands repeat door to door; the turntable is a plain box plinth and the books blank-spined boxes.

change.from: procedural wave-grain walnut, dark and matte; placeholder turntable and books
change.to: scanned walnut veneer, crown-cut and bookmatched across the three doors (grain continuous across the gaps), base colour lifted about 25%, satin lacquer at roughness about 0.3 so the top and doors pick up the window; a high-detail turntable (wood plinth, grooved record, real tonearm) and books with cloth spines and titles

changes.expected: Real figure and a soft sheen on the doors (median 60-80, lum range 18 or more), no repeated band pattern; the props hold up at 100%.

changes.problem: The oak floor is smooth and almost grainless, with hairline joints, no bevels and no reflections, so the pair stands on a CG surface.

evidence.measured: lum_range 8.4 in this 100-px patch and 7.6 in the sunlit patch [200,1350,300,1450]; at 2x the planks are flat colour bands; no reflection of the cabinets under either speaker.

change.to: scanned wide-plank natural oak (180-220 mm boards, 1.5-2.5 m lengths, real grain and the odd knot, at least 4K per 2 m), 1 mm micro-bevels, oiled satin finish at roughness 0.35-0.4 carrying soft blurred reflections of the window and the green cabinets

changes.expected: Grain reads at full size (100-px patches lum range 16 or more); a soft green reflection sits under each speaker.

changes.problem: The view out of the window is a flat beige block under a blank sky, a placeholder at the frame's bright edge.

evidence.measured: lum_median 216.4 with lum_range 1.0 (a flat fill); sky [10,20,90,300] median 243.6 with no detail.

change.from: flat beige block and plain sky
change.to: a real high-resolution exterior plate covering the whole left glazing (garden trees or a brick facade 15-25 m away), exposed about 1.5 stops over the interior wall, slightly soft, lit by the same low back-left sun

changes.expected: Detail through the glass (lum range 20 or more in the lower pane) without clipping; it reads as a real outside.

out_of_scope.request: Make the cabinets read as tinted acrylic over a white lining.
out_of_scope.why: The card specifies cabinets lined in white; the render shows see-through dark olive acrylic with the bracing and ports visible (front median 52.7-60.6, blue 16-18). That is the speaker asset's material, not the set or the light; check the product model.

out_of_scope.request: Verify the speakers' green against a colour reference.
out_of_scope.why: The card gives no reference hex and the cabinets render olive (median RGB 47,69,18; right horn wing 80,87,40) under the warm light. Supply the reference so colour truth can be tested with delta_e; if the tint itself is off, it is a product-asset fix.

out_of_scope.request: Give the woofer cloth covers a visible weave.
out_of_scope.why: The cloth discs read as flat plastic (lum range 7.8 left, 2.9 right); the cloth shader is part of the product. The raking sun in c1 will help reveal texture, but the material is fixed.
